Turn 2 explains :name parameter capture during tree traversal, building on the turn-1 findings instead of re-exploring the repository from scratch.
Distinguishes the internal routing-tree implementation from the public RouterGroup API, each with file-level evidence.

turns.question: Where are routes registered, and how are incoming requests matched to handlers?
turns.agentText:
I'll investigate the gin repo's source directly via GitHub's API/raw files without cloning.Now let me look at the radix tree implementation in tree.go, which handles the actual matching algorithm.Also confirming the middleware-chain mechanics briefly (`c.Next()` in context.go) since `handleHTTPRequest` calls it to actually invoke handlers.I have everything needed. Here's the full picture (verified against `gin-gonic/gin@34dac209`, default branch `master`, as of 2026-07-05).

## Route registration

**`routergroup.go`** — `RouterGroup` (methods `GET`, `POST`, `Handle`, `Any`, `Match`, `Static*`, `Group`, `Use`) is the public API apps call. Every verb method funnels into:

```go
func (group *RouterGroup) handle(httpMethod, relativePath string, handlers HandlersChain) IRoutes {
    absolutePath := group.calculateAbsolutePath(relativePath)
    handlers = group.combineHandlers(handlers)   // prepends group/global middleware
    group.engine.addRoute(httpMethod, absolutePath, handlers)
    ...
}
```
`Group()` returns a new `RouterGroup` sharing the same `*Engine`, with `basePath` and `Handlers` (middleware) composed via `calculateAbsolutePath`/`combineHandlers` — this is how nested groups and per-group middleware work.

**`gin.go`** — `Engine.addRoute(method, path, handlers)` (gin.go, in the `addRoute` func) is the actual registration point:
```go
root := engine.trees.get(method)   // one radix tree per HTTP method
if root == nil {
    root = new(node); root.fullPath = "/"
    engine.trees = append(engine.trees, methodTree{method: method, root: root})
}
root.addRoute(path, handlers)
```
`Engine.trees` is `methodTrees` — a slice of `{method string, root *node}`, i.e. **one radix tree per HTTP verb** (GET, POST, etc.), each tree holding its own set of registered paths/handlers.

## Tree construction (`tree.go`)

`(*node).addRoute` inserts a path into the method's radix tree, splitting nodes on longest common prefix (`longestCommonPrefix`), and `(*node).insertChild` handles `:param` and `*catchAll` wildcard segments (via `findWildcard`), enforcing rules like "only one wildcard per segment" and "catch-all must be at the end." Each `node` stores `path`, `indices` (first byte of each static child, for O(1)-ish dispatch), `wildChild`, `nType` (`static`/`root`/`param`/`catchAll`), and `handlers HandlersChain`.

## Request matching

**`gin.go: Engine.ServeHTTP`** (the `http.Handler` entry point) gets a pooled `*Context`, resets it, and calls `engine.handleHTTPRequest(c)`.

**`gin.go: handleHTTPRequest`** does the matching:
```go
t := engine.trees
for i := range t {
    if t[i].method != httpMethod { continue }
    root := t[i].root
    value := root.getValue(rPath, c.params, c.skippedNodes, unescape)
    if value.handlers != nil {
        c.handlers = value.handlers
        c.fullPath = value.fullPath
        c.Next()                     // runs the middleware+handler chain
        ...
        return
    }
    // else: trailing-slash redirect (RedirectTrailingSlash) or
    // case-insensitive fixed-path redirect (RedirectFixedPath) via redirectFixedPath/findCaseInsensitivePath
}
// HandleMethodNotAllowed -> 405, else NoRoute handlers -> 404
```

**`tree.go: (*node).getValue(path, params, skippedNodes, unescape) nodeValue`** is the core matcher: it walks the radix tree consuming the longest common prefix at each node, follows static children by first-byte lookup in `n.indices`, falls back to a `wildChild` (`:param` or `*catchAll`) when no static child matches, records extracted path parameters into `Params`, and uses a `skippedNodes` stack to backtrack when a greedy static match turns out to be a dead end (needed for correctness when both static and param children could match a prefix). It also computes `tsr` (trailing-slash-redirect) hints when no exact handler is found but one exists with/without a trailing slash.

**`context.go: (*Context).Next()`** executes the matched `HandlersChain` in order (`c.index++` loop calling `c.handlers[c.index](c)`), which is how middleware chains + the final route handler actually run; `Abort()` sets `c.index` to a sentinel `abortIndex` to short-circuit remaining handlers.

## Not verified
- I did not check `ginS` (the global default-engine wrapper package) or `examples/` — they're thin convenience wrappers over the same API, not separate logic.
- I did not run the test suite (`tree_test.go`, `routes_test.go`) to confirm behavior beyond reading source; the description above is from static reading of the code, not execution.
- I did not inspect `path.go` (`cleanPath`) or `internal/bytesconv` in depth — referenced only for their role (path cleaning, zero-copy byte/string conversion) as called from `gin.go`/`tree.go`.

turns.question: How are route parameters like :name captured during tree matching?
turns.agentText:
Route parameters are captured entirely in `tree.go`, in two phases: how the tree is built with a `param` node type, and how `getValue` extracts the actual value during matching.

## 1. Building the param node (`insertChild`)

When a route like `/user/:name` is registered, `findWildcard` scans the path for the first `:` or `*` and returns the wildcard token (e.g. `":name"`) plus its start index. In `(*node).insertChild`:

```go
if wildcard[0] == ':' { // param
    if i > 0 {
        n.path = path[:i]   // static prefix before the ':'
        path = path[i:]
    }
    child := &node{
        nType:    param,
        path:     wildcard,   // stores literally ":name"
        fullPath: fullPath,
    }
    n.addChild(child)
    n.wildChild = true
    n = child
    ...
}
```

So a `param` node's `path` field holds the raw `:name` string (colon included), and the parent is flagged `wildChild = true`. `addChild` (in `tree.go`) guarantees the wildcard child is always kept **last** in `n.children`, since param/catch-all matching is a fallback tried only after all static children fail.

## 2. Extracting the value at match time (`getValue`)

In `(*node).getValue`, once no static child's first byte matches (`n.indices` lookup fails) but `n.wildChild` is true, it falls to:

```go
n = n.children[len(n.children)-1]   // the wildcard child, always last
globalParamsCount++

switch n.nType {
case param:
    // Find param end (either '/' or path end)
    end := 0
    for end < len(path) && path[end] != '/' {
        end++
    }
    if params != nil {
        ...
        val := path[:end]
        if unescape {
            if v, err := url.QueryUnescape(val); err == nil { val = v }
        }
        (*value.params)[i] = Param{
            Key:   n.path[1:],   // strip leading ':' -> "name"
            Value: val,          // the matched segment
        }
    }
    // continue deeper if path remains, else check n.handlers
```

Key points:
- The captured value is just the path segment up to the next `/` or end-of-string (`end`).
- The key is `n.path[1:]` — the stored node path is `:name`, so stripping the first byte gives `name`.
- If `UnescapePathValues`/`UseEscapedPath` is set (passed down as `unescape` from `Engine.handleHTTPRequest`), the value goes through `url.QueryUnescape`.
- `Params` is a preallocated slice (`c.params`, capacity `engine.maxParams`, computed at registration time via `countParams` in `gin.go:addRoute`) that gets appended in place — this is why `Context.allocateContext` preallocates `Params` sized to `engine.maxParams`, avoiding per-request allocation.
- If there's more path left after the param segment (`end < len(path)`), matching continues into `n.children[0]` (whatever follows `:name` in the registered route, e.g. `/:name/profile`).

## Catch-all (`*filepath`) is the same mechanism, simpler

```go
case catchAll:
    val := path        // everything remaining, no '/' truncation
    ...
    (*value.params)[i] = Param{
        Key:   n.path[2:],   // node path is "/*filepath", strip "/*" 
        Value: val,
    }
    value.handlers = n.handlers
    return value
```
Catch-all consumes the rest of the path unconditionally (no truncation at `/`) and terminates the walk immediately — it must be the last segment (enforced at registration in `insertChild`).

## Where the result surfaces to user code
Back in `gin.go: handleHTTPRequest`:
```go
value := root.getValue(rPath, c.params, c.skippedNodes, unescape)
if value.params != nil {
    c.Params = *value.params
}
```
That's what `c.Param("name")` (in `context.go`, calling `c.Params.ByName`) reads from — a linear scan over the small `Params` slice (`Params.Get`/`ByName` in `tree.go`) rather than a map, since routes typically have very few params.

**Not verified**: I haven't traced `countParams`/`maxParams` sizing arithmetic in `gin.go` line-by-line beyond the `addRoute` snippet already shown, nor exercised this with an actual running Gin server to confirm behavior empirically — this is based on static reading of `tree.go`/`gin.go` source.
